tool_description: Get the basic metadata on all breeds of dogs from around the world. Check out encurate.app to manage content on your mobile apps. Contact to feature your app on encurate.app website.
name: DogBreedDB
title: DogBreedDB

api_list.name: Paginated
api_list.description: Get all dog breed results in a set of 10 per page.
api_list.code:
import requests

url = "https://dogbreeddb.p.rapidapi.com/paginated/"

headers = {
            "X-RapidAPI-Key": "SIGN-UP-FOR-KEY",
            "X-RapidAPI-Host": "dogbreeddb.p.rapidapi.com"
        }

response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
print(response.json())
api_list.convert_code:
import requests

url = "https://dogbreeddb.p.rapidapi.com/paginated/"

headers = {
            "X-RapidAPI-Key": "SIGN-UP-FOR-KEY",
            "X-RapidAPI-Host": "dogbreeddb.p.rapidapi.com"
        }

response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
print(response.json())

results.breedDescription: The Afador is a hybrid dog composed of an Afghan Hound and a Labrador Retriever that originated in Alaska around the year 2000.
The Affenhuahua is a mixed breed dog–a cross between the Chihuahua and Affenpinscher dog breeds.
The Affenpinscher, also known as the Monkey Terrier, is a terrier-like toy Pinscher breed of dog.
results.furColor: black, gray, silver, black and tan, red, brownish, orangey tan

results.breedDescription: The Afghan Hound is a hound that is distinguished by its thick, fine, silky coat and its tail with a ring curl at the end.
results.furColor: fawn, gold, brindle, white, red, cream, blue, gray, tricolour

results.breedDescription: The Airedale Terrier (often shortened to "Airedale"), also called Bingley Terrier and Waterside Terrier, is a dog breed of the terrier type that originated in the valley (dale) of the River Aire, in the West Riding of Yorkshire, England.
The Akbash, Turkish: Akbaş, is a traditional Turkish breed or type of flock guardian dog from western Anatolia.
The Akita is a historic dog breed of large size originating from the mountains of northern Japan.
The Akita Chow is a mixed breed dog–a cross between the Akita and Chow Chow dog breeds.
results.furColor: silver, fawn, red, black, brown, white

results.breedDescription: The Akita Pit is a mixed breed dog–a cross between the Akita and American Pit Bull Terrier dog breeds. Intelligent, protective, and loyal, these pups inherited some of the best traits from both of their parents.
An Akita Shepherd is a mixed breed dog–a cross between the Akita and German Shepherd Dog breeds.
results.furColor: brindle, white, silver, red, gray,brown, sable, black

api_list.name: Order by Descending

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Yorkshire Terrier is one of the smallest dog breeds of the terrier type and indeed of any dog breed. The breed developed during the 19th century in Yorkshire, England. Ideally its maximum size is 7 pounds.
test_endpoint.furColor: Blue & Tan, Black & Tan, Black & Gold, Blue & Gold

test_endpoint.breedDescription: A fun-loving “designer dog” — and therefore a mixed dog breed — a Yorkipoo is a cross between the Yorkshire Terrier and a Toy or Miniature Poodle. Intelligent, affectionate, and gentle, they make a delightful companion. They also fit in perfectly to apartment life, especially if you don’t mind the barking.
test_endpoint.furColor: Cream, Black, White, Red, Sable, Apricot, Tan, Chocolate, Gray, and Silver

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Yakutian Laika is an ancient working dog breed that originated in the Arctic seashore of the Sakha Republic. Yakutian Laikas are multipurpose laikas, able to herd reindeer, hunt game and pull a sled. They are registered with the Russian Kennel Club, the FCI and the AKC's Foundation Stock Service.
test_endpoint.furColor: Tri-colored with Black, White, and Brown, Black, White

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Xoloitzcuintle is one of several breeds of hairless dog. It is found in Estándar, Intermedio, and Miniatura sizes. The Xolo also comes in a coated variety, totally covered in fur. Coated and hairless can be born in the same litter as a result of the same combination of genes.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Gray-Black, Slate, Red, Liver or bronze

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Australian Kelpie, or simply Kelpie, is an Australian sheepdog capable of mustering and droving with little or no guidance. It is a medium-sized dog and comes in a variety of colours. The Kelpie has been exported throughout the world and is used to muster livestock, primarily sheep, cattle and goats.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Fawn, Chocolate, Cream, Black & Tan, Brown, Blue

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Wirehaired Pointing Griffon is a breed of dog used in hunting as a gundog. It is sometimes considered to be Dutch in ancestry, due to the nationality of the breed founder, Eduard Karel Korthals.
test_endpoint.furColor: Liver, Grey & Brown, Grey & Tan, White & Chocolate, Orange & White, Chestnut

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Whoodle is a mixed breed dog — a cross between the Soft-Coated Wheaten Terrier and Poodle dog breeds. Playful, friendly, and active, these pups inherited some of the best qualities from both of their parents. Whoodles also go by the names the Wheatendoodle, the Wheatenpoo, the Sweatendoodle, and the Sweatenpoo.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Brown, Red, Silver Grey, and Cream

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Whippet is a British dog breed of medium size. They are a sighthound breed that originated in England, where they descended from the Greyhound. Whippets today still strongly resemble a smaller Greyhound. Part of the hound group, Whippets have relatively few health problems other than arrhythmia.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, White, Brindle, Fawn, Blue, Red

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Westiepoo is a mixed breed dog — a cross between the West Highland White Terrier and Poodle dog breeds. Westiepoos are also sometimes known as Westiedoodles and Wee-Poos.
test_endpoint.furColor: White or Cream, Black or Tan

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The West Highland White Terrier, commonly known as the Westie, is a breed of dog from Scotland with a distinctive white harsh coat with a somewhat soft white undercoat. It is a medium-sized terrier, although with longer legs than other Scottish breeds of terrier.
test_endpoint.furColor: White

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Welsh Terrier originates from Wales and was originally bred for hunting fox, rodents and badger; but during the last century, it has mainly been bred for showing. Despite this, it has retained its terrier strength of character. The Welsh Terrier has been claimed to be the oldest existing dog breed in the UK.
test_endpoint.furColor: Tan and Black

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Welsh Springer Spaniel is a breed of dog and a member of the spaniel family. Thought to be comparable to the old Land Spaniel, they are similar to the English Springer Spaniel and historically have been referred to as both the Welsh Spaniel and the Welsh Cocker Spaniel.
test_endpoint.furColor: Dark, Rich Red and White

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Weimaraner is a large dog that was originally bred as a hunting dog in the early 19th century. Early Weimaraners were used by royalty for hunting large game such as boar, bear and deer.
test_endpoint.furColor: Mouse-Gray to Silver-Gray

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Vizsla is a dog breed from Hungary and belongs to the Federation Cynologique Internationale group 7, the Canadian Kennel Club group 1, and the American Kennel Club. The Hungarian or Magyar Vizsla or Smooth-Haired Vizsla are sporting dogs and loyal companions
test_endpoint.furColor: Solid golden rust

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Valley Bulldog is a mixed breed dog–a cross between the Boxer and English Bulldog breeds. Medium in size, active, and loyal, these pups inherited some of the best qualities from both of their parents. Valley Bulldogs also go by the name Bull Boxer.
test_endpoint.furColor: Red, Tan, Brindle, White, and Fawn

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Treeing Walker Coonhound is a breed of hound descended from the English and American Foxhounds. The breed originated in the United States when a stolen dog known as "Tennessee Lead" was crossed into the Walker Hound in the 19th century.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, White, Tri-color

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Treeing Tennessee Brindle is a breed of cur. Since 1995, its records have been maintained through the American Kennel Club's Foundation Stock Service Program.
test_endpoint.furColor: Brindle or Black with Brindle trim

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Transylvanian Hound is a dog breed originating from Hungary and Transylvania and was historically primarily used for hunting. It is a strong, medium-sized scent hound, characterized by a black body, with tan and sometimes white markings on the muzzle, chest and extremities, and distinctive tan eyebrow spots.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black coat with Tan spots

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Toy Fox Terrier is a small terrier breed of dog, directly descended from the larger Smooth Fox Terrier but since 1936, it has been registered in the USA with the UKC as a separate breed.
test_endpoint.furColor: White, Tricolor, White and Tan, White and Black

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Tosa Inu is a breed of dog of Japanese origin that is considered rare. It was originally bred in Tosa, Shikoku as a fighting dog and is the only breed still used in Japanese dog fighting. Ownership is restricted in some countries as a dangerous breed.
test_endpoint.furColor: Red or Fawn

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Tornjak, is a breed of livestock guardian dog native to Bosnia and Herzegovina. The name comes from the local word for a sheep pen, "tor". The foundation stock is made up from genetically homogeneous landrace shepherding dogs dispersed in the mountains and valleys of the region.
test_endpoint.furColor: Mix of Brown, Black, White, and Red

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Tibetan Terrier is a medium-sized breed of dog that originated in Tibet. Despite its name, it is not a member of the terrier group. The breed was given its English name by European travelers due to its resemblance to known terrier breeds.
test_endpoint.furColor: White, Gold, Tricolor, Brindle, Silver, Black

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Tibetan Spaniel is a breed of assertive, small dogs originating in Tibet. This breed is not a spaniel in the original meaning of the term; its breeding differs from other spaniels, and unlike true spaniels, which are gun dogs, the Tibetan spaniel is a companion dog.
test_endpoint.furColor: Any color or Mixture of colors

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Tibetan Mastiff is a large size Tibetan dog breed. Its double coat is medium to long, subject to climate, and found in a wide variety of colors, including solid black, black and tan, various shades of red and bluish-gray, and sometimes with white markings around neck, chest and legs.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Brown, Gold, and Blue, with or without Tan markings

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Thai Ridgeback is a dog from Thailand. The Thai Ridgeback is one of only three breeds that has a ridge of hair that runs along its back in the opposite direction to the rest of the coat. The other two are the Rhodesian Ridgeback and the Phu Quoc Ridgeback.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Fawn, Blue, Red

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Texas Heeler is a mixed breed dog–a cross between the Australian Cattle Dog and Australian Shepherd dog breeds. Texas Heelers get their name from the state where you’re most likely to find them–Texas–combined with the “Heeler” nickname of their Australian Cattle Dog parent (also called the Queensland Heeler or Blue Heeler).
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Blue Merle, and Blue Ticked with White or Fawn

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Terripoo is a cross between the Australian Terrier and the miniature Poodle. Intelligent, intuitive, and playful, these small dogs make excellent family pets. Terripoos are also known as Terri Poos, Terridoodles, and Terrypoos.
test_endpoint.furColor: Red, Cream, White, Brown, Tan, and Blue

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Taiwan Dog is a breed of small or medium dog indigenous to Taiwan. They are well-adapted to the uneven and thickly forested terrain of Taiwan, having become a semi-wild breed prior to the arrival of several colonial reigns and foreign powers.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, White, Fawn, and Brindle

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Swedish Vallhund, also known as the Västgötaspets and Swedish cow dog, is a breed of dog native to Sweden. The breed's name, Vallhund, when translated into English, means herding dog, as the Swedish Vallhund was originally bred as a drover and herder of cows over 1,000 years ago.
test_endpoint.furColor: Sable pattern of Gray to Red

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Swedish Lapphund is a breed of dog of the Spitz type from Sweden, one of three Lapphund breeds developed from a type of dog used by the Sami people for herding and guarding their reindeer.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Liver

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Sussex Spaniel is a breed of dog native to Sussex in southern England. It is a low, compact spaniel and is as old a breed as and similar in appearance to the Clumber Spaniel. They can be slow-paced, but can have a clownish and energetic temperament.
test_endpoint.furColor: Golden Liver

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Schnauzer or Standard Schnauzer is a dog breed that originated in Germany in at least 14th–15th century, of Schnauzer breed type and progenitor of the Giant Schnauzer and Miniature Schnauzer. Initially it was called Wire-Haired Pinscher, while Schnauzer was adopted in 1879.
test_endpoint.furColor: Pepper and Salt or Pure Black

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Staffy Bull Bullmastiff is a mixed breed dog — a cross between the Staffordshire Bull Terrier and the Bullmastiff breeds. Calm, devoted, and affectionate, these pups inherited some of the best qualities from both of their parents.
test_endpoint.furColor: Brindle, Fawn, Black, White, Brown, and Red

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Staffordshire Bull Terrier, commonly called the Staffy or Stafford, is a shorthaired, purebred dog breed of medium size that originated in the Black Country of Staffordshire in the English Midlands. It is in the terrier group, one of several group designations used by various breed registries.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, White, Brindle, Fawn, Brindle & White, Fawn & White, Black & White, Red & White, Blue, Red, Blue & White

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Stabyhoun, or Stabijhoun or Stabij, is one of the rarest dog breeds in the world. It hails from the Dutch province of Friesland; its origins lie in the forested region of eastern and southeastern Friesland.
test_endpoint.furColor: Roan, Black & White, White & Chocolate, Orange & White

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Springador is a mixed breed dog–a cross between the Springer Spaniel and Labrador Retriever dog breeds. Loyal, friendly and smart, these pups inherited some of the best qualities from both of their parents.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Brown, and Gold

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Spinone Italiano is an Italian breed of hunting dog, traditionally used for tracking, for pointing and for retrieving game.
test_endpoint.furColor: White, Brown Roan, Orange Roan, Orange & White

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Spanish Water Dog breed is used in Spain as a general purpose sheepdog and guard. It is also used sometimes as a gundog, and is skilled at retrieval from water.
test_endpoint.furColor: Beige, Black, White, and Brown

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Spanish Mastiff or Mastín Español is a breed of dog from Spain, originally bred to be a guard dog and whose specialized purpose is to be a livestock guardian dog protecting flocks and/or herds from wolves and other predators.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black to Fawn, Red, Brindle, Tri-colored

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Soft-coated Wheaten Terrier is a pure-breed terrier originating from Ireland. Wheatens typically have one of two coat types: Irish or Heavy. The Irish coat is generally silkier and wavier than the Heavy, or American coat, which is thicker and fuller.
test_endpoint.furColor: Shades of Wheaten, Pale Beige, Shimmering Gold

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Small Münsterländer is a versatile hunting-pointing-retrieving dog breed that reached its current form in the area around Münster, Germany. The Large Münsterländer is from the same area, but was developed from different breeding stock and is not related as the names would suggest.
test_endpoint.furColor: Brown-and-White coat

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Slovenský kopov is a medium-sized breed of hunting dog of the scenthound type. The breed originated in Slovakia, in Central Europe, and is bred for boar hunting. The name Black Forest Hound seems to have been created in North America for marketing purposes, since the breed has no connection with the Black Forest.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black coat, Tan spots

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Slovak Cuvac is a Slovak breed of dog, bred for use as a livestock guard dog. This breed—also known as Slovensky Cuvac, Slovak Chuvach, Tatransky Cuvac and Slovensky Kuvac—is closely related to the Hungarian Kuvasz. The alternate German and English spelling Tchouvatch reflects the pronunciation: chew-votch.
test_endpoint.furColor: White

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Slovak Rough-haired Pointer is a gundog breed developed after World War II in Slovakia. It is known by many confusingly similar names in English, including the Slovak Wirehaired Pointer, the Slovak Pointing Griffon, the Slovak Wirehaired Pointing Griffon, and the Slovak Wirehaired Pointing Dog. Its closest relative is the Bulgarian Hound.
test_endpoint.furColor: Shades and Tints of Grey

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Sloughi, or Arabian Greyhound, is an ancient breed of domesticated dog, specifically a member of the sighthound family. It originates from North Africa and is found in Algeria, Tunisia, Morocco and Libya.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Brindle, Fawn, Sandy
test_endpoint.origin: Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, North Africa, Libya

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Skye Terrier is a breed of dog that is a long, low, hardy terrier and "one of the most endangered native dog breeds in the United Kingdom" according to The Kennel Club.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Blue, Dark or Light Gray, Silver Platinum, Fawn, or Cream

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Australian Silky Terrier or simply Silky Terrier is a small breed of dog of the terrier dog type. The breed was developed in Australia, although the ancestral types and breeds were from Great Britain. It is closely related to the Australian Terrier and the Yorkshire Terrier.
test_endpoint.furColor: Blue & Tan, Silver & Tan, Grey & Tan, Silver Black & Tan, Black & Tan

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Silken Windhound is an American breed of sighthound. Like most sighthounds, Silkens are noted coursers.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, White, Brindle, Black & Tan, Sable, Red

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Siberian Husky is a medium-sized working sled dog breed. The breed belongs to the Spitz genetic family. It is recognizable by its thickly furred double coat, erect triangular ears, and distinctive markings, and is smaller than the similar-looking Alaskan Malamute.
test_endpoint.furColor: White, Black, Black & Tan, Gray & White, Silver-gray, Black & White, Sable & White, Red & White, Grey

test_endpoint.breedDescription: A shorkie, also commonly known as a shorkie tzu, is a crossbreed between a shih tzu and a Yorkshire terrier, resulting in a spunky, loyal little fluffball. Shih poos possess all the charm and personality of both the shih tzu and toy poodle along with the hypoallergenic coat of the poodle.
test_endpoint.furColor: Blue, Black, Brown, Fawn, Red, and White

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Shollie is a mixed breed dog — a cross between the German Shepherd Dog and Border Collie dog breeds. Intelligent, energetic, and loyal, these pups inherited some of the best qualities from both of their parents.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Brown, Golden, and White

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Shiranian is a mixed breed dog — a cross between the Shih Tzu and Pomeranian breeds. Small, adorable, and loyal, these pups inherited some of the best qualities from both of their parents. Shiranians are also called Pomshi, Shih-Pom, Shih-A-Pom and Pom-Tzu.
test_endpoint.furColor: Brown, Black, Sable, Brindle, Red, and White

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Shiloh Shepherd has a combination of German Shepherd and Alaskan Malamute in their genetic makeup. The developer wanted to create a dog similar to the German Shepherd, but larger in size and with a softer and more gentle nature. The Shiloh Shepherd is currently recognized by: ACA = American Canine Association.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black & Tan, Cream, Dark Brown, Golden, Silver, Red

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Shikoku Inu or Kōchi-ken is a Japanese breed of dog from Shikoku island. It was designated as a national monument in 1937.
test_endpoint.furColor: Red, Red-sesame, and Blackish or Black-sesame

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Shih-Poo is a mixed breed dog — a cross between the Shih Tzu and Toy Poodle dog breeds. Small, hypoallergenic and cuddly companions, these pups inherited some of the best qualities from both of their parents.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, White, Brown, Brindle

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Shih Tzu is a toy dog breed originating from Tibet and having been bred from the Pekingese and the Lhasa Apso. Shih Tzus are well known for their short snout and large round eyes, as well as their ever growing coat, floppy ears, and short and stout posture.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Black and White, Gray and White, or Red and White

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Shichon is a mixed breed dog–a cross between the Shih Tzu and the Bichon Frise dog breeds. Affectionate, intelligent, and outgoing, these pups inherited some of the best qualities from both of their parents.
test_endpoint.furColor: Cream, Silver, Black and White, Brown and White, and Chocolate

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Shiba Inu is a breed of hunting dog from Japan. A small-to-medium breed, it is the smallest of the six original and distinct spitz breeds of dog native to Japan. A small, alert, and agile dog that copes very well with mountainous terrain and hiking trails, the Shiba Inu was originally bred for hunting.
test_endpoint.furColor: Red Sesame, Black & Tan, Cream, Black Sesame, Red, Sesame

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Shetland Sheepdog, often known as the Sheltie, is a breed of herding dog that originated in the Shetland Islands of Scotland. The original name was Shetland Collie, but this caused controversy amongst Rough Collie breeders of the time, so the breed's name was formally changed.
test_endpoint.furColor: Merle, Blue Merle, Tri-color, Sable & White, Sable, Black & White, Black & Tan

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Shepsky is a mixed breed dog–a cross between the German Shepherd and Siberian Husky dog breeds. Medium in size, energetic, and loyal, these pups inherited some of the best qualities from both of their parents.
test_endpoint.furColor: Brown, Black, Cream, White, Red, and Blue

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Sheepadoodle is a mixed breed dog — a cross between the Old English Sheepdog and Poodle dog breeds. Smart, playful, and loving, these pups inherited some of the best traits from both of their parents.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Black and White, Gray

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Segugio Italiano dog breed originated in Italy back in ancient times to work as a scenthound during hunts. Today, people know this medium-sized breed as an energetic and sociable companion.
test_endpoint.furColor: Brown, Pied, Fawn, and Red

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Sealyham Terrier is a rare Welsh breed of small to medium-sized terrier that originated in Wales as a working dog. It is principally a white-bodied, rough-coated breed, developed in the mid-to-late-19th century by Captain John Edwardes at Sealyham House, Pembrokeshire.
test_endpoint.furColor: White, White & Chocolate, Lemon & White, Badger & White, Blue & White

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Scottish Terrier (Scottish Gaelic: Abhag Albannach; also known as the Aberdeen Terrier), popularly called the Scottie, is a breed of dog. Initially one of the highland breeds of terrier that were grouped under the name of Skye Terrier, it is one of five breeds of terrier that originated in Scotland, the other four being the modern Skye, Cairn, Dandie Dinmont, and West Highland White terriers.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Brindle, Wheaten

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Scottish Deerhound, or simply the Deerhound, is a large breed of sighthound, once bred to hunt the red deer by coursing. In outward appearance, the Scottish Deerhound is similar to the Greyhound, but larger and more heavily boned with a rough-coat.
test_endpoint.furColor: Gark gray, Brindle, Light gray, Red fawn, Sandy red, or Yellow

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Schnoodle is a cross between a Miniature Schnauzer and a Poodle. Schnoodles are charming, funny and smart, and their alert nature — thanks to that double dose of Schnauzer and Poodle attentiveness — makes them excellent watchdogs. They are small dogs and typically have a curly coat that must be clipped regularly.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Gray, Silver, Brown, White, Apricot, Sable, Black and White, Black and Tan, and even parti-color

test_endpoint.breedDescription: Your Schnocker hybrid is a mix of the Miniature Schnauzer and the Cocker Spaniel and, as such, can inherit the appearance traits from either or both parent breeds. Breeders and owners of the Schnocker hybrid describe her as a small to medium-sized canine who stands 12 to 15 inches tall and weighs 16 to 25 pounds
test_endpoint.furColor: Brown, Black, Cream, Grey and White

test_endpoint.breedDescription: A Schipperke is a small breed of dog that originated since the 1600's in Belgium. There has been a long informal debate over whether this type of dog is a spitz or miniature sheepdog. In their home country of Belgium they are considered a small shepherd.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Apricot, Chocolate, Cream, Black & Tan, Blue

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Schapendoes or Dutch Sheepdog, is a breed of dog originating in the Netherlands. The Schapendoes was originally a herding dog and general farm dog, but today also participates in dog sports such as agility and flyball.
test_endpoint.furColor: White, Black, Gray, Silver, Brown, Red, Apricot, and Tan, or any combination of those colors

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Samusky is a mixed breed dog–a cross between the Samoyed and the Siberian Husky dog breeds. Highly intelligent, loyal, and good-natured, these pups inherited some of the best qualities from both of their parents. The Samusky goes by several other names, including Samsky or simply Samoyed Husky mix.
test_endpoint.furColor: White, Cream, Fawn, Gray, Red, Sable, and agouti

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Samoyed is a breed of medium-sized herding dogs with thick, white, double-layer coats. They are a spitz-type dog which takes its name from the Samoyedic peoples of Siberia. Descending from the Nenets Herding Laika, they are a domesticated animal that assists in herding, hunting, protection and sled-pulling.
test_endpoint.furColor: White, White and Biscuit, Cream

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Saluki, also known as the Persian Greyhound, is a standardised breed developed from sighthounds – dogs that hunt primarily by sight rather than scent – that was once used by nomadic tribes to run down game animals. The dog was originally bred in the Fertile Crescent.
test_endpoint.furColor: White, Cream, Fawn, Red, Grizzle/Tan, Black/Tan, and Tri-color (white, black and tan)

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Saint Bernard or St. Bernard is a breed of very large working dog from the Western Alps in Italy and Switzerland. They were originally bred for rescue work by the hospice of the Great St Bernard Pass on the Italian-Swiss border.
test_endpoint.furColor: Shades of Red with White or White with Red

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Saint Berdoodle is a mixed breed dog — a cross between the Saint Bernard and Poodle dog breeds. Friendly, intelligent, and loyal, Saint Berdoodles are great family dogs. The Saint Berdoodle is also known as the Saint Berpoo, St. Berpoo, and St. Berdoodle.
test_endpoint.furColor: White-and-Brown and White-and-Black

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Russian Tsvetnaya Bolonka, also known as the Bolonka Zwetna in Germany, or known simply as a Bolonka is a rare toy breed of the Bichon type, developed in Moscow and Saint Petersburg, Russia, from the ancestors of smaller dogs such as the Bichon Frise, Toy Poodle, Shih Tzu, Pekingese and French Bolognese.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Brown, Gray, "Wolfgray," Blue, Cream, Silver, Fawn, and Red

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Rottweiler is a breed of domestic dog, regarded as medium-to-large or large. The dogs were known in German as Rottweiler Metzgerhund, meaning Rottweil butchers' dogs, because their main use was to herd livestock and pull carts laden with butchered meat to market.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black with marking of rust or mahogany

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Rottle is a mixed breed dog — a cross between the Rottweiler and Poodle dog breeds. Playful, intelligent, and eager to please, these pups inherited some of the best qualities from both of their parents.
test_endpoint.furColor: Brown, Black, White, Red, Gray, and Blue

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Rottador is a mixed breed dog–a cross between the Rottweiler and Labrador Retriever dog breeds. Large, energetic, and loyal, these pups inherited some of the best qualities from both of their parents. The Rottador is also called the Labrottie, Labweiller, Rottwador and Rott 'n Lab.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Brown, and Grey or combination

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Romanian Mioritic Shepherd is a large breed of livestock guardian dog that originated in the Carpathian Mountains of Romania.
test_endpoint.furColor: White, Piebald, Grey

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Rhodesian Ridgeback is a large scenthound and sighthound dog breed bred in the Southern Africa region. Its forebears can be traced to the semi-domesticated ridged hunting and guardian dogs of the Khoikhoi. These were interbred with European dogs by the early colonists of the Cape Colony of southern Africa.
test_endpoint.furColor: Light Wheaten to Red Wheaten

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Redbone Coonhound is an American breed of hunting dog. It may be used to hunt raccoon, deer, bear, boar, cougar, or other large game. It originated in the Southern United States, and derives from foxhounds brought by immigrants from Scotland. It is characterized by its deep red coat.
test_endpoint.furColor: Solid red or chestnut; white is allowed on the paws and chest

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Rat Terrier is an American dog breed with a background as a farm dog and hunting companion. They share much ancestry with the small hunting dogs known as feists. Common throughout family farms in the 1920s and 1930s, they are now recognized by the United and American Kennel Clubs and are considered a rare breed.
test_endpoint.furColor: White, Black with Tan or Rust, White and Black or Tan, Red, Lemon, Blue, Chocolate and Orange

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Rafeiro do Alentejo is a Portuguese breed of livestock guardian dog. It is named for its area of origin, the Alentejo region of southern Portugal. It is recognised by the Clube Português de Canicultura, and was definitively accepted by the Fédération Cynologique Internationale in 1954.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Fawn, or Brindle

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Pyrenean Sheepdog, the Chien de Berger des Pyrénées in French, is a small to medium-sized breed of herding dog from the Pyrenees Mountains region of France. It is found herding flocks of sheep throughout the Pyrenees alongside the much larger Pyrenean Mountain Dog which is kept as a flock guardian.
test_endpoint.furColor: Gray; Blue Merle; Brindle; Black; and Black with White markings, Fawn, Tan, Copper

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Pyrenean Mastiff or Mastín del Pirineo is a Spanish breed of large livestock guardian dog from the autonomous community of Aragón in north-eastern Spain. It was traditionally used to protect flocks during the annual transhumance to high summer pasture in the Pyrenees.
test_endpoint.furColor: White and Beige, White and Black, White and Brown, White and Silver

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Pyredoodle is a mixed breed dog–a cross between the Great Pyrenees and Standard Poodle dog breeds. Calm, fearless, and loyal, these pups inherited some of the best traits from both of their parents.
test_endpoint.furColor: Gray, White, Apricot, Cream, and Black

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Puli is a small-medium breed of Hungarian herding and livestock guarding dog known for its long, corded coat. The tight curls of the coat appear similar to dreadlocks. A similar-looking, but much larger breed – also Hungarian – is the Komondor. Plural form of Puli is Pulik in Hungarian.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Brownish, White, Gray

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Puginese is a mixed breed dog–a cross between the Pug and Pekingese dog breeds. Affectionate, sensitive, and independent, these pups inherited some of the best traits from both of their parents. Puginese dogs go by a few different names, including Pekeapug and Pugapeke.
test_endpoint.furColor: Cream, Brown, Gray, Black, or Brindle

test_endpoint.breedDescription: A puggle is a dog crossbred from a pug and a beagle. The puggle was first bred by designer dog breeders in the United States with the aim of producing a healthy companion dog that is less likely to inherit some health and behavioural issues common in the parent breeds.
test_endpoint.furColor: Fawn, Red, Tan, Lemon, Black

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The pugalier is a hybrid of a pug and a cavalier king charles spaniel. They are bred to retain the basic features of a pug with a slightly longer nose in an attempt to reduce the breathing problems that pugs are notorious for. They have become increasingly popular over the last 5-10 years.
test_endpoint.furColor: Apricot, Black, Brown, Ruby, Gray, White, Black & Tan, and Tricolor

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The pug is a breed of dog originally from China, with physically distinctive features of a wrinkly, short-muzzled face and curled tail.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Fawn, Silver Fawn, Apricot

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Pudelpointer is a versatile hunting dog breed from Germany. It is a pointing breed that came from a cross between the German hunting poodle and the English Pointer.
test_endpoint.furColor: Brown, Brownish Red, or Black

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Portuguese Water Dog originated from the Algarve region of Portugal. From there the breed expanded to all around Portugal's coast, where they were taught to herd fish into fishermen's nets, retrieve lost tackle or broken nets, and act as couriers from ship to ship, or ship to shore.
test_endpoint.furColor: Shades of Brown, or Black or Brown with White

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Portuguese Sheepdog is a medium-sized breed of dog of the herding dog type, and is one of the indigenous regional dogs of Portugal. The Portuguese name refers to Serra de Aires, a mountain near Montforte in the Alentejo region. The breed is nicknamed cão macaco for its furry face and lively attitude.
test_endpoint.furColor: Yellow, Black, Gray, and Fawn

test_endpoint.breedDescription: A Portuguese Pointer, is a breed of dog developed as a gun dog. It is one of several pointing breeds and is mainly used in red-legged partridge hunting.
test_endpoint.furColor: Fawn or Red with Cream accents

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Portuguese Podengo, also known as the Podengo Português or Portuguese Warren Hound, is hound breed from Portugal. As a breed, the Podengo is divided into three size categories that are not interbred: small, medium and large. Their coats are either short and 'smooth', or longer and 'wired'.
test_endpoint.furColor: Light, Medium, or Dark Yellow or Fawn, Light, Medium, or Dark Yellow or Fawn

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Porcelaine is a breed of dog originating from France. In 1844, this scent hound was originally called “Briquets Francs Comtois” and named after a French region bordering Switzerland.
test_endpoint.furColor: Spotted White

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Poodle, called the Pudel in German and the Caniche in French, is a breed of water dog. The breed is divided into four varieties based on size, the Standard Poodle, Medium Poodle, Miniature Poodle and Toy Poodle, although the Medium Poodle variety is not universally recognised.
test_endpoint.furColor: Blue, Black, White, Gray, Silver, Brown, Café-au-lait, Apricot, and Cream

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Poochon is a mixed breed dog–a cross between the Toy Poodle and Bichon Frise dog breeds. Small, happy, and intelligent, these pups inherited some of the best qualities from both of their parents. Researching their parents can offer much insight into their personalities and characteristics.
test_endpoint.furColor: Cream, Tan, and Apricot

test_endpoint.breedDescription: Cute, silly, and suited for apartment life, the Pomsky is a dog who likes to be the center of attention, and with their adorable looks and playful antics, they often get the adoration they crave.
test_endpoint.furColor: Grey and White, Brown or Reddish Brown, Blue, Pure White

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Pomeranian is a breed of dog of the Spitz type that is named for the Pomerania region in north-west Poland and north-east Germany in Central Europe. Classed as a toy dog breed because of its small size, the Pomeranian is descended from larger Spitz-type dogs, specifically the German Spitz.
test_endpoint.furColor: White, Black, Red, Blue, Cream, Grey-shaded, Tan, Orange, Brown

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Pomeagle is a mixed breed dog — a cross between the Pomeranian and Beagle dog breeds. Small, affectionate, and curious by nature, these pups inherited some of the best qualities from both of their parents.
test_endpoint.furColor: Brown, Red, Fawn, Cream, White, Brindle, Black, and Sable

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Pomchi is a mixed-breed dog — a cross between the Pomeranian and the Chihuahua dog breeds. Playful, devoted, and energetic, these small pups inherited some of the best qualities from both of their parents. Pomchis go by several names, including Pomahuahua, Chimeranian, Chi-Pom, and Pom-Chi.
test_endpoint.furColor: Sable and Brown, Blue and Tan, Black and Tan, or Cream

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Pomapoo is a mixed breed dog — a cross between the Pomeranian and Toy Poodle dog breeds. Compact, intelligent, and affectionate, these pups inherited some of the best qualities from both of their parents.
test_endpoint.furColor: Brown, Black, White, Red, Fawn, and Sable

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Polish Lowland Sheepdog, is a medium-sized, shaggy-coated, sheep dog breed native to Poland.
test_endpoint.furColor: White with Black, Gray, or Sandy patches; or Gray with White or Chocolate

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Pointer, sometimes called the English Pointer, is a medium-sized breed of pointing dog developed in England.
test_endpoint.furColor: Liver (dark brown), Black, Orange, or Lemon

test_endpoint.breedDescription: Smaller than the average Beagle dog breed, these compact scenthounds are merry and fun-loving. But the Pocket Beagle is still a hound and, as such, requires patience and creative training techniques to overcome their sometimes stubborn nature.
test_endpoint.furColor: White or Cream, Black, Tan, Lemon, Red, Brown, Liver, Blue, and Gray

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The pack-hunting Plott dog breed was developed in North Carolina more than 200 years ago to hunt bear and wild boar. They are still used as hunting dogs today and have proven their worth as pack hunters. They also participate in tracking and other dog sports.
test_endpoint.furColor: Brindle, Tan, Chocolate, Yellow, Buckskin, Chocolate, Orange, Gray, Blue, Liver, Brown, and Black

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Pitsky is a mixed breed dog — a cross between the American Pit Bull Terrier and Siberian Husky dog breeds. They range in size from medium to large, they are energetic, and loyal, these pups inherited some of the best qualities from both of their parents
test_endpoint.furColor: White, Black, Brown, Grey, Brindle

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Pharaoh Hound or Kelb tal-Fenek is a Maltese breed of hunting dog. It is traditionally used for rabbit-hunting in the rocky terrain of the islands; the Maltese name means "rabbit dog".
test_endpoint.furColor: Rich Tan to a Chestnut Tan

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Petit Basset Griffon Vendéen, or PBGV, is a breed of dog of the scent hound type, bred to trail hares in bramble-filled terrain of the Vendée district of France. The breed is known in the United States as "Petit" or "PBGV," in England as "Roughie," and in Denmark as "Griffon" or "Petit".
test_endpoint.furColor: White with any combination of Lemon, Orange, Black, Tri-colour or Grizzle markings

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Presa Canario is a Spanish breed of large dog of mastiff or catch dog type. It originates in the autonomous region of the Canary Islands, and is found mostly in the islands of Gran Canaria and Tenerife. It was formerly known as the Dogo Canario.
test_endpoint.furColor: Mix of Black, Brindle, Tan, and Silver

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Pembroke Welsh Corgi is a cattle herding dog breed that originated in Pembrokeshire, Wales. It is one of two breeds known as a Welsh Corgi. Pembroke Welsh Corgis descended from the Spitz family of dogs
test_endpoint.furColor: Fawn, Black & Tan, Sable, Black & White, Red

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Pekingese is a breed of toy dog, originating in China. The breed was favored by royalty of the Chinese Imperial court as both a lap dog and companion dog, and its name refers to the city of Peking where the Forbidden City is located.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black and Tan, Fawn or Red Brindle, and Particolor

test_endpoint.breedDescription: A Peekapoo is hybrid dog breed — a cross between the Pekingese and Poodle breeds. The mix makes for a wonderful companion dog who will spend their days perched on your lap or sitting by your side.
test_endpoint.furColor: Silver, Gray, White, Sable, Red, Cream, Apricot, Chocolate, to Buff and Black

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Patterdale Terrier is a breed of dog descended from the Northern terrier breeds of the early 18th century.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Black & Tan, Blue & Tan, Chocolate, Red

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Papipoo is a mixed breed dog — a cross between the Papillon and Poodle dog breeds. Loving, intelligent, and active, this devoted, little dog wants to be part of all family activities. Papipoos are also known as Papoodles, Papi Doodles, Papidoodles, and Papi Poos.
test_endpoint.furColor: White, Black, Cream, Red, Sable, Apricot, and Gray

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Papillon, also called the Continental Toy Spaniel, is a breed of dog, of the spaniel type. One of the oldest of the toy spaniels, it derives its name from its characteristic butterfly-like look of the long and fringed hair on the ears. A Papillon with dropped ears is called a Phalene.
test_endpoint.furColor: Parti-colored, White with patches of any color

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Otterhound is a British dog breed. It is a scent hound and is currently recognized by the Kennel Club as a Vulnerable Native Breed with around 600 animals worldwide.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Tan Grizzle, White

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Old English Sheepdog is a large breed of dog that emerged in England from early types of herding dog. Obsolete names for the breed include Shepherd's Dog and bob-tailed sheep-dog. The nickname Bob-tail originates from how dogs of the breed traditionally had their tails docked.
test_endpoint.furColor: Gray, Grizzle, Blue or Blue Merle, Brown, and Fawn

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever is a medium-sized gundog bred primarily for hunting. It is often referred to as a "toller". It is the smallest of the retrievers, and is often mistaken for a small Golden Retriever. Tollers are intelligent, eager to please, alert, and energetic
test_endpoint.furColor: Red, Orange with white markings

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Norwich Terrier is a breed of dog originating in the United Kingdom, and was bred to hunt small rodents. With a friendly personality, Norwich Terriers are today mostly a companion dog breed.
test_endpoint.furColor: Grizzle, Wheaten, Black & Tan, Tan, Red

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Norwegian Lundehund is a small dog breed of the Spitz type that originates from Norway. Its name is a compound noun composed of the elements lunde, meaning puffin, and hund, meaning dog.
test_endpoint.furColor: Reddish Brown, Fawn, Black, Gray

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Norwegian Elkhound is one of the Northern Spitz-type breed of dog and is the National Dog of Norway. The Elkhound has served as a hunter, guardian, herder, and defender. It is known for its courage in tracking and hunting moose and other large game, such as bears or wolves.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black and white coloring, often noted as grey or silver

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Norwegian Buhund is a breed of dog of the spitz type. It is closely related to the Icelandic Sheepdog and the Jämthund. The Buhund is used as a watch dog and an all purpose farm and herding dog.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Wheaten, Red Wheaten

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Northern Inuit Dog, along with its offshoot breed lines the Tamaskan dog, the British Timber dog and the Utonagan, is a breed of dog developed from a 1980s breeding project in the United Kingdom with the objective of producing a dog breed that resembles wolves.
test_endpoint.furColor: White, Black, Grey, Sable, and Apricot

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Norfolk Terrier is a British breed of dog. Prior to gaining recognition as an independent breed in 1964, it was a variety of the Norwich Terrier, distinguished from the "prick eared" Norwich by its "drop ears". Together, the Norfolk and Norwich Terriers are the smallest of the working terriers.
test_endpoint.furColor: Grizzle, Wheaten, Black & Tan, Red

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Newfoundland is a large working dog. They can be black, brown, grey, or white. However, in the Dominion of Newfoundland, before it became part of the confederation of Canada, only black and Landseer coloured dogs were considered to be proper members of the breed.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Brown, Gray, or Landseer

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Neapolitan Mastiff or Mastino Napoletano is an Italian breed of large dog. It descends from the traditional guard dogs of central Italy. It was recognised as a breed by the Ente Nazionale della Cinofilia Italiana in 1949, and accepted by the Fédération Cynologique Internationale in 1956.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Brindle, Tawny, Blue, Mahogany

test_endpoint.breedDescription: A Mutt or mixed breed dog is a testament to nature. Without any input — some might say interference — from humans, the mixed breed defies description. Available in all sizes, shapes, colors, and patterns, they might have a long snout or a short nose. They may display pointed ears or floppy ones. They could have a stubby tail, spindly legs, a giant spot over their left eye — or all three.
test_endpoint.furColor: Brown, White, Black

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Mudi is a herding dog breed from Hungary. It is closely related to the Puli and Pumi, from which it was separated in the 1930s. They continue to be used in herding, as well as participating in a variety of dog sports.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Brown, White, Fawn, Grey, or a Marbled mix of Black and Grey

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Treeing Feist is a breed of feist from the Southeastern United States. Originally considered a single breed, the Mountain Feist is now considered a separate breed with both being separately recognized by the United Kennel Club.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, White, Gray, Silver, Blue, Tan, Red, Brown, Cream, Sable, Brindle, Pied, Isabella, and Fawn

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Mountain Cur is a type of working dog that is bred specifically for treeing and trailing small game, like squirrel and raccoons. They are also used for hunting and baying big game like bear and wild boar as well as being an all-purpose farm dog.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Tan, Brown, Yellow, Brindle, and Black and Brindle

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Morkie is a mixed breed dog–a cross between the Maltese and the Yorkshire Terrier dog breeds. Small, energetic, and super silly, these pups inherited some of the best qualities from both their parents. This crossbreed is usually referred to as the Morkie, but it is sometimes called the Morkshire Terrier.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Brown, White

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Miniature Schnauzer is a breed of medium dog of the Schnauzer type that originated in Germany in the mid-to-late 19th century.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, White, Salt & Pepper, Black & Silver

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Miniature Pinscher, also known as the Zwergpinscher, and Min Pin, is a small breed of dog of the pinscher type originating in Germany. The breed's earliest ancestors may have included the German Pinscher mixed with Italian greyhounds and dachshunds
test_endpoint.furColor: Black & Rust, Stag Red, Chocolate & Rust, Black & Tan, Chocolate & Tan, Red

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The English Mastiff, or simply the Mastiff, is a British dog breed of very large size. Likely descended from the ancient Alaunt and Pugnaces Britanniae, with a significant input from the Alpine Mastiff in the 19th century.
test_endpoint.furColor: Fawn, Apricot, or Brindle

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Mastador is a mixed breed dog — a cross between the Mastiff and Labrador Retriever dog breeds. Large, energetic, and lovable, these pups inherited some of the best qualities from both of their parents. Mastador can also be spelled Mastidor.
test_endpoint.furColor: Brown, Black, Yellow and Brindle

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Maremma Sheepdog is considered an “Old World European” breed, sharing ancestry with other Eastern European livestock guardian dogs, especially mountain-dwelling dogs, like the Pyrenean Mountain Dog and Kuvasz.
test_endpoint.furColor: Tinge of Yellow, Peach, or Orange

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Manchester Terrier is a breed of dog of the smooth-haired terrier type. It was first bred in the 19th century to control vermin, notably rats, at which it excelled.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Black & Tan, Tan, Blue & Tan, Blue

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Maltipoo (aka Multipoo, maltepoo) is a hybrid mix between a maltese and a poodle. The Maltipoo has a playful and affectionate nature.
test_endpoint.furColor: Cream, White, and Silver

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Maltese Shih Tzu, also known as the Mal-Shi, Malti zu, and the Malt-Tzu, is a hybrid or mixed dog breed — a cross between the Maltese and Shih Tzu breeds. Created with the same goal as Doodles — to be a small, allergy-friendly companion who doesn’t shed much — this hybrid is a sweet lapdog who likes to play with the kids.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Brown, Black and White, Brown and White, and Black and Brown

test_endpoint.breedDescription: Maltese dog refers both to an ancient variety of dwarf canine generally associated with the island of Malta, and to a modern breed of dog in the toy group. The contemporary variety is genetically related to the Bichon, Bolognese, and Havanese breeds.
test_endpoint.furColor: Pure white

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Löwchen or Little Lion Dog is a breed of small dog. The Löwchen once had the dubious distinction, like the Portuguese Water Dog and the Havanese, of being the rarest dog in the world. In 1973 there were only 65 registered examples of the breed.
test_endpoint.furColor: Cream, White, Gray, Black

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Lhasapoo is a mixed breed dog–a cross between the Lhasa Apso and Poodle dog breeds. Protective, loyal, and playful, these pups inherited some of the best qualities from both of their parents. Lhasapoos also go by the names Lhasadoodle or just Lhasa Apso Poodle mix.
test_endpoint.furColor: Brown Black, White, Grey, Apricot, and Cream

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Lhasa Apso is a non-sporting dog breed originating in Tibet. It has traditionally been used as an interior sentinel.
test_endpoint.furColor: Honey, Black, White, Slate, or Parti-color

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Leonberger is a dog breed, whose name derives from the city of Leonberg in Baden-Württemberg, Germany.
test_endpoint.furColor: Lion-yellow, Golden to Reddish-brown

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Lapponian Herder is a breed of dog from Finland, one of three Lapphund breeds developed from a type of dog used by the Sami people for herding and guarding their reindeer.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Brown, and Grey

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Lancashire Heeler is a small breed of dog developed for use as a drover and herder of cattle. The Lancashire Heeler is listed by the Kennel Club as a vulnerable breed.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Liver, Tan

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Lakeland Terrier is a dog breed, which takes its name from its place of origin, the Lake District in England. The dog is a small to mid-size member of the Terrier family. While independent in personality, it interacts well with owners and all family members, and is mostly hypo-allergenic.
test_endpoint.furColor: Blue, Black, Liver (a deep reddish-brown), Red, and Wheaten (pale yellow or fawn)

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Lagotto Romagnolo is an Italian breed of dog. It originates in the marshlands of the Delta del Po in the eastern part of the Romagna sub-region of Italy. The name derives from Romagnol can lagòt, meaning "water dog"
test_endpoint.furColor: Cream, Brown, Orange, or Golden

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Labsky is a mixed breed dog — a cross between the Labrador Retriever and Siberian Husky dog breeds. Active, smart, and loyal, these pups inherited some of the best qualities from both of their parents. Labskies also go by the name Huskador.
test_endpoint.furColor: White, Black, Yellow, Brown, Red and Grey

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Labrastaff is a mixed breed dog — a cross between the Labrador Retriever and Staffordshire Bull Terrier dog breeds.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Brown, and Brindle

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Labrador Retriever or Labrador is a British breed of retriever gun dog. It was developed in the United Kingdom from fishing dogs imported from the colony of Newfoundland, and was named after the Labrador region of that colony.
test_endpoint.furColor: Chocolate, Black, and Yellow

test_endpoint.breedDescription: A Labradoodle is a crossbreed dog created by crossing the Labrador Retriever and the Standard, Miniature, or Toy poodle. The term first appeared in 1955, but was not initially popular.
test_endpoint.furColor: Gold, Apricot, Caramel, Chalk, Black, Red, Café, Cream, Silver, Chocolate, Parchment, and Blue

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Labradane is a mixed breed dog — a cross between the Labrador Retriever and Great Dane dog breeds. Loyal, affectionate, and playful, these pups inherited some of the best qualities from both of their parents.
test_endpoint.furColor: Brown, Black, and White

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Labrabull is a mixed breed dog — a cross between the American Pit Bull Terrier and the Labrador Retriever dog breeds. Medium in size, energetic, and loyal, these pups inherited some of the best qualities from both of their parents. Labrabulls are also called Pitadors.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, White, Gray, Brown, Yellow and Silver

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Labmaraner is a mixed breed dog — a cross between the Labrador Retriever and Weimaraner dog breeds.
test_endpoint.furColor: Brown, Yellow, Black, and Grey

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Labernese is a mixed breed dog — a cross between the Labrador Retriever and Bernese Mountain Dog breeds.
test_endpoint.furColor: Chocolate, White, and Yellow

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Lab Pointer is a mixed breed dog — a cross between the Labrador Retriever and Pointer dog breeds. Energetic, loyal, and intelligent, these pups inherited some of the best qualities from both of their parents. Lab Pointers are also sometimes known as Pointerdors
test_endpoint.furColor: Creamy white, Brown, and Black

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Kyi-Leo is a mixed breed dog — a cross between the Maltese and Lhasa Apso dog breeds. Playful, lively, and sweet, these pups inherited some of the best qualities from both of their parents. Kyi-Leos are also known as Maltese Lion Dogs.
test_endpoint.furColor: Black, Silver, Tan, White

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Kuvasz is a traditional Hungarian breed of flock guardian dog. Mention of the breed can be found in old Hungarian texts. They have historically been royal guard dogs, or guarded livestock, but have been increasingly found in homes as pets over the last seventy years.
test_endpoint.furColor: White

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Kromfohrländer commonly known as Kromi is a breed of dog that originated in Germany. It is used as a companion dog. Particularly long lived, reaching 17-18 years old regularly. Very attached to their owners, often being described as a "one-person dog".
test_endpoint.furColor: White, Light brown, Dark brown, and Tan

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Jindo dog is an indigenous dog native to Jindo Island in South Korea. It is one of South Korea's Natural Treasures, prized for its loyalty and homing instinct.
test_endpoint.furColor: White, Fawn, Red, Brindle, Grey, Black, and Black and Tan

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Kooikerhondje is a small spaniel-type breed of dog of Dutch ancestry that was originally used as a working dog, particularly in an eendenkooi to lure ducks. Kooikers were popular in the 17th and 18th century and appear in the paintings of Rembrandt and Jan Steen.
test_endpoint.furColor: Orange, Deep chestnut red, White

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Komondor also known as the Hungarian sheepdog, is a large, white-coloured Hungarian breed of livestock guardian dog with a long, corded coat.
test_endpoint.furColor: Cream, White

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Kishu, sometimes called Kishu Inu or Kishu dog, is a Japanese breed of dog. It is descended from ancient medium-sized breeds and named after the Kishu region, now Mie Prefecture and Wakayama Prefecture. This breed is similar to the Hokkaido, Shikoku and the Kai Ken
test_endpoint.furColor: White. Brindle, Red

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The King Shepherd is a hybrid dog breed. They're a mix of many different breeds, but always have German Shepherd ancestry. The main colors of King Shepherds are fawn, red, black, brown, and sable. Their coats are usually a combination of two or more colors.
test_endpoint.furColor: Fawn, Red, Black, Brown, and Sable

test_endpoint.breedDescription: The Maremma Sheepdog is considered an “Old World European” breed, sharing ancestry with other Eastern European livestock guardian dogs, especially mountain-dwelling dogs, like the Pyrenean Mountain Dog and Kuvasz.
